speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by understanding your symptoms. When you walk, do you feel like you are drunk, or do your legs feel weak and shaky? Additionally, how long have you been experiencing these gait and limb ataxia issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That "drunken" appearance suggests a cerebellar issue. Is there a history of head trauma, recent headaches, or vision changes like double vision on the right side? Also, do you have any history of alcohol use or diabetes? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital signs are within normal ranges (Temperature: Normothermic, Blood Pressure: Within normal range, Heart Rate: Within normal range, Respiratory Rate: Within normal range). Neurological examination reveals an ataxic gait, evidence of ataxia on coordination tests, and right upper limb strength of 4/5. MRI Brain findings show multifocal demyelinating lesions on T1/T2 images without gadolinium enhancement, consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML).
